    The Manufacturing AI Research Center was newly established on January 1, 2024, as a direct organization under the Vice President of the Korea Institute of Industrial Technology. It aims to concentrate capabilities on developing an AI platform for the "AI-based innovation in manufacturing" initiative, promoting the rapid dissemination of the developed platform, and fostering in-house AI experts.

    Hong-In Won, Ph.D.

    Principal Researcher · Korea Institute of Industrial Technology

    Researcher Profile

    Hong-In Won, Ph.D.

    Principal Researcher, Korea Institute of Industrial Technology (KITECH)
    Head of the Manufacturing AI Cooperation Team

    Dr. Hong-In Won is a Principal Researcher at KITECH. Since 2019, he has served as a KITECH research principal investigator, working across manufacturing AI, digital transformation, and data-driven production systems. He received his Ph.D. in Mechanical Design Engineering from Hanyang University and previously worked as a postdoctoral researcher at TU Dresden.

    Contact

    Research Focus

    Manufacturing AI

    AI methods and implementation strategies for practical manufacturing innovation and industrial digital transformation.

    Digital Twin Systems

    Data, simulation, and virtual validation approaches for intelligent production systems.

    Data-Driven Production

    Process intelligence, quality-oriented analytics, and collaborative deployment of AI in production environments.

    Selected Research Outputs and Engagement

    Selected External Engagements

    • Unite Seoul 2026 — industry presentation, “A Unity Digital Twin-based Synthetic Data Pipeline for Manufacturing AI.”
    • KOREATECH Future Technology Education Center Faculty Training (2026) — “Building and Applying Multi-Agent Systems in the AI Agent Era.”
    • Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology (2026) — invited workshop, “The Evolution of AI Agent Engineering.”

    Professional Leadership & Service

    • Joint Faculty Member, Hanyang University Graduate School (2026–2027).
    • Executive Director and Academic Committee Member, Korean Society for Noise and Vibration Engineering.
    • Expert Committee Member for equipment-diagnosis qualification and training evaluation.

    Selected Research Outputs

    • “Adaptive Task Token Framework for Multi-Agent Logistics Operations.” IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2026. Accepted for publication.
    • “Digital twin-based test-time adaptation for robust visual perception in manufacturing.” Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence, 2026.
    • “AI-driven multivariate time series forecasting of transmembrane pressure in ultrafiltration: A stationarity-aware approach.” Journal of Water Process Engineering, 2025.
    • “FALCON: Fine-grained Alignment for Counting Objects in Industry.” Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, 2026.
    • “Digital Twin-based Robust Viewpoint Sampling for Automated Robotic Inspection.” IEEE International Conference on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems, 2026.
